The openat2 support probe and proc-record reader close their acquired descriptor after the tested post-acquisition MemoryError and KeyboardInterrupt injections. Confined replacement preserves a foreign PID-named O_EXCL collision, reports APPLICATION_UNKNOWN when a raising rename leaves application observationally ambiguous, removes every tested invocation-owned temporary path, and permits the tested exact retries. The hygiene gate treats the live-gate registry and whole-program artifact binding helper as critical in isolation and excludes superseded packets from current selection. Authority remains checker-owned NONE and the value-movement closure remains deliberately red.

nonclaims: This packet is bounded to the named deterministic Python exception injections, replacement fault matrix, and hygiene-selection cases. It does not establish universal BaseException safety, arbitrary bytecode-interruption safety, or a filesystem crash theorem.

APPLICATION_UNKNOWN means the checker cannot attribute application after a raising rename. It does not claim application or durability; callers refuse success and the tested desired-byte retry is idempotent.
Persistent close or unlink failures, hostile concurrent in-process descriptor or pathname manipulation, abrupt process death, kernel faults, and cross-platform behavior remain outside this claim.
Supersession removes predecessor packets from current-evidence selection while preserving their bytes for historical replay. It does not alter historical facts or validate their overbroad wording.
